complexity.notes: Correct because the delimiter lies outside the 256-character ASCII set the problem guarantees, so it can never appear inside an input string. It would break under the statement's Unicode follow-up, where a ||length-prefix encoding (e.g. `len#string` per element)|| works for arbitrary characters without needing a forbidden delimiter. `output.pop(-1)` could be written more idiomatically as `s.split("😀")[:-1]`.
complexity.summary: Joins the strings with a non-ASCII emoji delimiter (plus a trailing delimiter) and splits on it to decode, popping the empty tail left by the trailing separator.
